report.headline: Play-making guard projected for a smaller but still functional NBA role; the shooting-efficiency projection itself is not trustworthy

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to fall to 18.7% in the NBA from 23.9% in the 2015-16 EuroLeague season, landing just below the league-average usage of 20.0% for the target NBA season.

risks.text: Turnover rate was 16.3% in the source season, a meaningful cost alongside the high assist rate.
The projection is built on a modest sample of 31 games and 1,031 minutes in the source season, limiting how much weight the underlying rate stats can bear.

The true shooting projection of 54.7% should not be treated as informative: the model's error on this metric (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the NBA league-mean true shooting of 55.1%, meaning it is worse than or equal to a trivial baseline.

Even for usage, where the model does beat the trivial baseline (3.3% error vs. 4.3% for league_mean), the 80% interval still spans about 10.6 points of usage, roughly twice the league's standard deviation.

strengths.text: Elite playmaking translated to a 31.4% assist rate and 6.0 assists per 75 possessions in the source season.
Scored efficiently at volume, posting 17.6 points per 75 possessions in the EuroLeague.
Usage stood 0.84 standard deviations above the EuroLeague average, indicating a well-above-average offensive role even before accounting for league difficulty.
True shooting sat 0.66 standard deviations above the EuroLeague average in the source season, at 61.2%.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 13.4% to 24.0% and the 95% interval from 10.6% to 26.8%, a span of roughly two standard deviations of NBA usage (sd 5.3%); this estimate rests on only 61 historical EL->NBA transitions, so the model can rank this player against peers but cannot price his individual role precisely.
